parts.label: (i)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Use correct quotient or product rule. [M1]
Obtain correct derivative in any form, e.g. $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{-3\sin x(2+\sin x)-3\cos x\cos x}{(2+\sin x)^2}$. Condone invisible brackets if recovery is implied later. [A1]
Equate numerator to zero. [M1]
Use $\cos^2x+\sin^2x=1$ and solve for $\sin x$, e.g. $-6\sin x-3=0$. [M1]
Obtain coordinates $x=-\pi/6$ and $y=3$, ISW; from correct working, no others in range. [A1+A1]
SR: a candidate who only states the numerator of the derivative, but justifies this, can have full marks; otherwise M0A0M1M1A0A0. Total 6.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
State indefinite integral of the form $k\ln(2+\sin x)$. [M1*]
Substitute limits correctly, equate result to 1 and obtain $3\ln(2+\sin a)-3\ln2=1$, or equivalent. [A1]
Use correct method to solve for $a$. Allow correct method on an incorrect equation if that equation has a solution. Guidance: $1+\tfrac12\sin a=e^{1/3}\Rightarrow a=\sin^{-1}[2(e^{1/3}-1)]$; can be implied by 52.3°. [M1(dep*)]
Obtain $a=0.913$ or better. Ignore additional solutions; must be in radians. [A1] Total 4.
